subject: pgvector approximate-nearest-neighbor comparison

decision.reason: The currently registered real product corpus contains only eight documents. An exact-vs-HNSW-vs-IVFFlat comparison at this size would not answer a current product scale question, so PR #1 requires deferral rather than manufacturing an ANN winner.

supportingEvidence.role: adversarial filtered ANN recall and isolation evidence
supportingEvidence.limitation: The fixture deliberately forces exact/HNSW variants to measure filtered recall and leakage; it sets productionIndexSelected=false and cannot select the production access path.
The presence of dimension-specific HNSW indexes makes them planner-eligible; it does not prove that PostgreSQL uses one for every production query.
The runtime supplies authorization/truth filters plus ORDER BY <=> LIMIT without an explicit exact/HNSW/IVFFlat hint, leaving the physical plan to PostgreSQL.
Synthetic fixed-dimensional vectors and three timing samples per target are not real-corpus semantic quality evidence and are not used to select a production ANN index.

reevaluateWhen: A materially larger production-like registered corpus is available.
Measured exact-vector retrieval latency on that corpus creates a concrete scale question.
Recall@10, latency, build time, index size, RAM and incremental-update cost can all be measured on the same held-out corpus.

runtimeExecution.queryContract: Authorize and constrain generation/space/vault/lifecycle/trust before ORDER BY embedding <=> query LIMIT; PostgreSQL chooses the physical access path.
runtimeExecution.claimBoundary: AKP does not report EXACT_SCAN, HNSW or IVFFlat as the production strategy unless a representative benchmark and an observed plan justify that decision.
